title: FLaG: Fine-Grained Latent Grouping for Hallucination Detection

problem.claim: Hallucinations in large language models arise from heterogeneous failure mechanisms, making reliable detection difficult for a single global uncertainty score.

gap.claim: Hallucination detection needs to interpret diverse representation- and token-level signals under multiple latent explanations.

contributions.claim: FLaG models correctness through multiple latent evidence groups for hallucination detection.
FLaG softly routes instances to multiple groups using energy-based routing and combines group-conditional reliability signals through log-marginal aggregation.
The framework connects its aggregation rule to optimal evidence aggregation under heterogeneous error mechanisms and provides a tractable approximation with a controllable error bound.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that FLaG captures heterogeneous hallucination patterns while remaining invariant to decision thresholds and evaluation metrics.
The authors report that FLaG operates as a frozen-model head, requires no modification to the underlying language model, and incurs minimal computational overhead.
Across multiple benchmarks and LLM backbones, the authors report SOTA performance, robust transfer across datasets and models, and effectiveness under limited supervision.

narrative_sequence.summary: Heterogeneous hallucination mechanisms make detection by a single global uncertainty score unreliable.
The task is formulated as mechanism-aware aggregation of diverse signals under latent explanations.
FLaG uses latent evidence groups, soft energy-based routing, and log-marginal aggregation.
The design is reported to handle heterogeneous patterns, remain threshold- and metric-invariant, and operate as a lightweight frozen-model head.
The authors connect the method to Bayes-optimal aggregation and report strong benchmark, transfer, and limited-supervision results.

source_observation.claim: The method aggregates reliability signals conditionally on multiple latent evidence groups.

interpretation.claim: When failure mechanisms are heterogeneous, routing evidence through latent subgroups may be more suitable than relying on one global score.

application.claim: Use mechanism-aware or subgroup-conditional evidence aggregation when signals may reflect distinct underlying failure modes.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether latent grouping improves every dataset, model, or deployment setting.

source_observation.claim: The framework is designed as a frozen-model head with minimal computational overhead.

interpretation.claim: A detection layer that avoids modifying the underlying model may reduce integration cost.

application.claim: Consider frozen-model auxiliary heads when adding reliability detection to deployed language models.

exception.claim: The abstract does not provide the overhead, latency, or resource requirements needed to assess deployment suitability.

unknowns: Specific benchmarks, LLM backbones, datasets, metrics, and numerical results are not provided.
The supervision regimes and limited-supervision quantities are not specified.
The controllable error bound is not quantified.
Implementation details and reproducibility information are not provided.
